steps.text: Melt butter in a large skillet over medium heat. Stir in garlic and cook for a few seconds until fragrant.

Arrange scallops in a single layer in the skillet; cook until golden brown on one side, about 2 minutes. Turn scallops over using tongs and continue cooking until firm and opaque, about 2 minutes more.
Transfer scallops to a platter, reserving butter in the skillet.
Whisk lemon juice, salt, and pepper into butter; pour sauce over scallops to serve.

raw_recipe.headline: Easy Garlic-Lemon Scallops
raw_recipe.description: This scallop recipe makes deliciously tender sautéed scallops with a buttery lemon-garlic pan sauce for a restaurant-worthy meal that's easy to make!

video.description: Simple recipe packed with flavor. Scallops sautéed in creamy butter and garlic, then once fragrant taken to a platter to pour extra lemon juice, butter, salt and pepper over scallops to serve. Pair with angel hair pasta and your favorite Pinot gris!

review.reviewBody: I made some changes - first I infused some olive oil with garlic, I removed the garlic and seared the scallops in the oil on high heat. Once the scallops were done I transfered them to a plate. Then I added the butter and sauteed some garlic and shallots and added about 2 tablespoons of flour (as a thinkening agent for sauce). Then added some chicken stock and w-wine, lemon, pasta, asparagus, tomatoes, parmesan and of course the scallops and tossed it all together. So good!!! I guess I came up with my own recipe, but thanks for the good start.

Don't add the garlic before the scallops! Scallops should be cooked on medium high to high heat (you want them browned after all- "No color, no flavor" as Gordon Ramsay says), and this just means the garlic burns badly in the butter while the scallops cook. I trusted the recipe, and had to quickly heat up and add butter to another pan to transfer the scallops to before they got burned garlic taste on them. If done again I would add the garlic after I'd turned removed the scallops and turned down the heat. Then add the lemon juice and seasonings. Otherwise simple and tasty.

The recipe was good but needed a tiny bit of pizazz to become great.

I reduced the butter to 1 stick (1/3 Cup) which was plenty, and added a cup of chopped flat italian parsley and allowed to bubble and soften, then added garlic careful not to burn. Then added the rest of the ingredients along with a 1/4 tsp of tiny shredded lemon zest. Once the scallops were browned on both sides, I flabayed the dish with about a 1/2 of suaveningon blanc (white wine). I loved it and the kids loved it.

These scallops are an easy weeknight family dinner. I may also try them over angel hair pasta as an app for company. The recipe's deliciousness is inversely proportional to its easiness - which in my mind is pretty much the perfect combo. And speaking of perfect pairings, we had it with a burgundy-style sauvignon blanc, dry and lemony. We followed some of Mia's tweaks, sauteeing shallots in with the garlic, adding white wine, plus a little flour to make a creamier sauce. We also added more lemon than the recipe calls for. At the table, we topped it with fresh grated parmesan and a sprinkle of crushed red pepper. Parsley would have been great, too, if we'd had it on hand. Thanks for giving us a new family fave!

Olive oil for half the butter.Garlic salt, Lemon Pepper, Old Bay, and White Pepper. I added a little bit of Riesling. I also poured it over the pasta (Linguini or your choice, Angel Hair). Sauce: Leftover sauce from scallops. 1/2 cup of the starched pasta water, zest of 3 lemons and juice, and 1/2 a stick of butter for the sauce and put it all together. Maybe drizzle a little bit of olive oil with it. When it's cooked, Don't forget (store bought parmesan) 1/2 cup. mix that in with a little olive oil. Then served with scallops over the pasta with fresh Parmesan on top .

Excellent recipe. My version: Cooked garlic in mixture of butter & olive oil. Removed garlic. Sauted scallops, added salt and a dash of red pepper flakes and some dried parlsey. Removed scallops when ALMOST done. Added lemon juice to the pan along with a little chicken broth & fresh broccoli flowers. Covered and steamed broccoli until crisp tender. Returned scallops to pan along with some cooked pasta. Heated very slowly until all ingredients were warm. EXCELLENT & so easy. The red pepper flakes do kick it up a bit, but just use a little. Be careful not to overcook the scallops.

This was very good, very easy. I slightly browned the garlic in the butter, added the small scallops. After about 4 minutes I added some chicken broth and parsley and lemon juice, just to make it saucier. I had to add Wondra gravy flour to thicken my extra sauce, then served it all over fettucine. I'll make it again, with more garlic and probably cilantro rather than parsley.

I modified the recipe for 2 servings. I had 12 sea scallops and used half-stick (1/4 c), 3 cloves garlic, juice of half a lemon. I also added a little w-wine and capers. The scallops turned out delicious.
Easy great recipe. We loved it! My only suggestion is to dry your scallops on paper towels before adding to pan.

I added1/4 a cup of pine nuts.
Toast the pine nuts in the skillet in a small amount of the butter until golden brown.
Then add the rest of the butter and follow the remainder of the recipe.

Used this basic recipe and it was amazing! I did change things up a bit though. First, I halved the recipe for just the 2 of us and cooked and crumbled a few bacon strips. After searing the scallops and removing them so they did not become over-cooked, I added the bacon, lemon juice, about 1/2 cup chicken broth and about the same amount of chardonnay, 2 chopped green onions and served on spaghetti with freshly grated Parmesan cheese. Served with a colorful salad with raspberry vinaigrette and a crunchy bread. Have absolutely never had anything so beautiful or tasty in any restaurant that served scallops in my life! Thanks for the wonderful basic recipe and the suggestions of many reviewers!
Super easy and tasty. I served over pasta. I used more lemon juice because I like lemon, but the recipe is fine as is.

Very good! Like a lot of folks I jazzed this up a bit with pancetta, white wine, chicken stock, flour for a roux, and s shallot with the garlic. Also putting over angel hair and parmesan to top it off as well as incorporate with the sauce. I will probably change up the cook the next time but it turned out very good.
I didn’t change a thing. More garlic next time.
Cooked for about 1-1/2 minutes a side, and they were perfectly tender. Nothing to change, just follow the recipe for quick-and-easy scallops that are absolutely delicious.
Very easy, very bland. Next time, I'll add lemon zest, and do some of the things the other reviewers have suggested.
Easy, elegant, DELICIOUS!
I found stirring worked well for smaller scallops
Was so good! Quick and easy! Perfect for Valentine's dinner at home!
Loved everything! Easy to make, so flavorful and perfect with steamed rice
